cards.text: This one's a song, baker: a Psalm of Asaph, the man whose name is on it, set to a tune called The Lilies of the Covenant. Don't ask me to hum it, because my mustache starts flapping like it's trying to take off. Asaph opens with “Hear us,” and pictures God leading Joseph, meaning Joseph's descendants, like a flock.

cards.question: Asaph pictures God's people as a flock. So what does he call God? O ___ of Israel
This Shepherd of Israel is also a King on a throne. Where does Asaph say God sits enthroned?

cards.text: Asaph asks God to shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, three of the tribes of Israel. That's not a quiet little prayer from the back, baker. That's a man standing on the counter going “OVER HERE!”

cards.question: Asaph has asked the Shepherd of Israel to shine forth. What does he ask God to do with His mighty power?

answers.text: Rally it and come save us
Hold it back a while longer
Turn it on the far mountains

cards.text: Then comes a line Asaph sings more than once, so lean in: “Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.” Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark junk drawer, so “shine upon us” hits me RIGHT here.

cards.question: When Asaph asks God to cause His face to shine upon His people, what is he really asking for?

answers.text: For God to look on them with favor
For a brighter morning to come soon
For a sign to appear in the sky

cards.text: Now Asaph calls Him the LORD God of Hosts. And he asks the question every waiting person asks, and baker, I waited in a junk drawer for years, so trust me, I KNOW this one: how long?

cards.question: Asaph asks the LORD God of Hosts how long something will go on. What is it?

answers.text: His anger smoldering against their prayers
The famine spreading across the land
The war with the armies of Egypt

cards.text: Then Asaph describes what life has been like for God's people. Let's just say nobody's asking for seconds.

cards.question: What does Asaph say God has given His people to eat and drink?

answers.text: Bread of tears and tears to drink
Ashes for bread and bitter water

cards.text: And it's not just trouble at home. Asaph says God makes them contend with their neighbors, like a group chat where every single reply starts a new fight.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says their enemies are leaving them alone.

cards.text: And here's that line again, with one addition: “Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.” Asaph's not done asking. Not even close.
Now Asaph changes pictures. No more sheep, baker, and I know, I was getting attached too. God's people are a vine, and Asaph tells its story from the day God uprooted it.

cards.question: Asaph says God uprooted this vine and moved it somewhere new. Where did God pull it up from?
True or false: Asaph says God transplanted the vine into empty land where no nations lived.

cards.text: God clears the ground for it Himself. Baker, I've cleared a LOT of countertops for a batch, but never a whole land.

cards.question: With the ground cleared, Asaph says the vine took ___ and filled the land

cards.text: This vine grows like dough you forgot about overnight. Its shade covers the mountains, and its branches cover the mighty cedars.

cards.question: Asaph's vine keeps on growing. How far does it send out its branches?

cards.text: Then the song turns. Asaph has a WHY for God, and it's a big one.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says the people's enemies are the ones who broke down the vine's walls.
With the walls down, everyone passing by picks the vine's fruit. What comes out of the forest to ravage it?

cards.text: But Asaph doesn't stop at why. He turns it into a request and tacks on a “we pray!” Baker, when a man says please with an exclamation point, he MEANS it.

cards.question: What does Asaph ask the God of Hosts to do for the vine?

answers.text: Return and look down from heaven
Tear the old vine out for good
Plant a brand new vine instead

cards.text: Asaph reminds God this vine is the root His own right hand planted. Then he calls it something new: “the son You have raised up for Yourself.” Baker, that vine just went from the garden to the FAMILY.

Then comes the hardest line in the song, about that same vine: “Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.” Friend, I've pulled burnt batches out of the oven before, and not one of them sat as heavy as that line.
Then Asaph turns from the vine to one person, the son of man, and says God raised him up for Himself, the same way he talked about the vine. Keep your eye on this one, baker.

cards.question: Asaph asks God to let His hand be upon the son of man. Where does Asaph say this man is?
Asaph asks God to let His hand be upon the man at His right hand. True or false: Asaph says then the people will not turn away from God.
Asaph asks God to revive His people. If He does, what will they do?

cards.text: Asaph closes with that line one last time, and this time he calls on the LORD God of Hosts: “Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.”
